BiblicalUsage: This word for a body of servants — a household staff — occurs twice. Isaac has 'great store of servants' alongside his flocks and herds, and the Philistines envy him; Job has 'a very great household' alongside his seven thousand sheep and three thousand camels, and he is 'the greatest of all the men of the east'.
TheologicalSignificance: Both men are measured by their households, and both lose them — Isaac by envy, Job by calamity. I believe the word is a quiet warning about wealth: a great household is a sign of God's blessing, and it is also the first thing envy and suffering take aim at.
RelatedEvents: Isaac in Gerar; Job's Suffering and Restoration
